chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with the Salam (advance payment for goods) in animals when their teeth (age) are described.

key_terms.أَسْنَانُهَا: Its teeth: Used here as a metonym for age, as the condition of teeth indicates the age of an animal.
key_terms.السَّلَمِ: Salam: A forward sale contract where the price is paid in advance and the goods are delivered later.
key_terms.الْحَيَوَانِ: Animals: Specifically referring to livestock or animals used in trade.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of Salam in animals according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), validates the Salam contract for livestock by anchoring its validity in the precise description of teeth, a standard biological indicator of age in classical Arab commerce. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing gharar (uncertainty) through tangible, observable characteristics, ensuring that the deferred delivery of the specific animal is clearly defined. It underscores the practical application of commercial flexibility in early Islamic jurisprudence, allowing for advance payment while maintaining contractual certainty.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem with the submission of the advance payment regarding the animals, when its age has been described’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Advance payment to buy an animal is not unlawful if the age of animals is clearly described.’”
